intro: Spanish is a language that you can read out loud. Its five vowels say one sound each. Once you know them, you can say new words right away.
In this unit, you will meet a friend named Ana and a llama named Yoyo. You will learn the vowels. You will learn the special letters h, j, ll, ñ and rr.
By the end, you can say hola and adiós. You can clap the beats in a word. You can read a new Spanish word before you know what it means.
bigQuestion: How do the sounds of Spanish help you read any word out loud?

timeline.t: Say hola to a new friend
Learn the sound of a: ah
Sing the five vowels: ah, eh, ee, oh, oo
Read a new word by its letters
Meet the quiet h and the strong j
Say ll like y and ñ like ny
Roll the rr in perro and say adiós

words.d: hi or hello — the h is quiet: OH-lah
goodbye — say ah-dee-OHS
mom — each a says ah
the bear — each o says oh
the butterfly — four beats: ma-ri-po-sa
the llama — the ll says y: YAH-mah
the boy — the ñ says ny: NEE-nyoh
the dog — roll the rr: PEH-rrroh

test.q: What sound does the Spanish a make?
choices: a short a, like in cat
test.why: The Spanish a always says ah.

test.q: What sound does the Spanish u make?
test.why: The Spanish u always says oo.

test.q: How many claps does mariposa have?

test.why: The h is quiet in Spanish.
Perro with a rolled rr means dog. Pero means but.
The ñ says ny, like in canyon.
The Spanish j sounds like a strong h.

test.q: How do you say the Spanish word me?

write.prompt: Say or write 3 sentences in Spanish. Greet a friend, tell your name, and say goodbye. For example: ¡Hola! Me llamo Ana. ¡Adiós! Use your own name.
tips: Put ¡ at the start and ! at the end.
Remember the accent mark on the o in adiós.
Read it aloud and say every vowel the Spanish way.

title: Sounds of Spanish

chapters.title: Five Vowels, Five Sounds
chapters.bigQuestion: How can you read a Spanish word out loud the first time you see it?

story.title: Ana Says Her Name
story.kicker: A new friend has a name that sounds the same both ways.
paragraphs: A new girl comes to class on Monday. She smiles and waves. She says, "¡Hola! Me llamo Ana." That means "Hi! My name is Ana."
Ana writes her name on the board. A-N-A. She says it slowly: ah-nah. Then she reads it from the end to the start. It is still Ana!
Ana tells us a secret. In Spanish, the letter a says ah every time. So the name sounds the same both ways. Every a in Ana says ah.
At the end of the day, Ana waves again. She says, "¡Adiós!" That means "Goodbye!" We wave back and say it too: ah-dee-OHS.
story.think: Can you think of another name that reads the same from the end to the start?

lessons.title: The Sound of A
lessons.mainIdea: In Spanish, the letter a always says ah, like in mamá.
reading: Say *mamá* (mom). Open your mouth wide. Say ah. Ma-má has two a sounds. Both say ah.
Now say *papá* (dad). It has two a sounds too. Each a says ah. In Spanish, a never changes its sound.
In English, a can make many sounds. Think of cat, cake and car. In Spanish, a only says ah.

words.d: mom — both a letters say ah: mah-MAH
dad — both a letters say ah: pah-PAH

look.title: Ah, Ah, Ah
look.text: Picture a doctor. The doctor says, "Open wide and say ah." That is the Spanish a. Now say mamá: mah-MAH. Now say papá: pah-PAH. Now say Ana: AH-nah.
look.prompt: Say mamá and papá. Does every a sound the same?

check.q: What sound does the Spanish a make?
choices: ah, like when the doctor checks your throat
a short a, like in cat
check.why: The Spanish a always says ah, in every word.
Mamá means mom. Papá means dad.
Each a says ah, so papá sounds like pah-PAH.

lessons.title: E, I, O and U
lessons.mainIdea: The five vowels say ah, eh, ee, oh, oo, and they never change.
reading: Spanish has five vowels: a, e, i, o, u. Each one has one sound. It says that sound every time.
A says ah. E says eh, like in pet. I says ee, like in see. O says oh. U says oo, like in moon.
Try *oso* (bear): OH-soh. Try *uva* (grape): OO-vah. The o and the u never change.

words.d: the bear — both o letters say oh: OH-soh
the grape — the u says oo: OO-vah

look.title: The Vowel Song
look.text: Sing it slowly. A says ah. E says eh. I says ee. O says oh. U says oo. Now sing it fast: ah, eh, ee, oh, oo! Clap one time for each sound.
look.prompt: Sing the five sounds. Which one makes your lips round?

check.q: What sound does the Spanish i make?
check.why: The Spanish i always says ee.
El oso is the bear. La uva is the grape.

check.q: What sound does the Spanish u make?
check.why: The Spanish u always says oo.

lessons.title: Say Every Letter
lessons.mainIdea: Spanish words sound the way they are spelled.
reading: In Spanish, you can read a new word out loud. Just say each letter's sound. Vowels never trick you.
Look at *la isla* (the island). The s is easy. I says ee. A says ah. Say it: EES-lah.
In English, many letters are quiet. In Spanish, the vowels always speak. Say every one.

words.d: the island — say EES-lah; the i says ee

look.title: Sound It Out
look.text: Look at a new word: luna. L says l. U says oo. N says n. A says ah. Put it together: LOO-nah. Luna means moon. You read it before you knew it!
look.prompt: Sound out the word mesa, one letter at a time.

check.why: The i says ee and the a says ah, so isla is EES-lah.
La isla means the island.

check.q: Why can you read a new Spanish word out loud?
choices: Each vowel always makes the same sound
check.why: Spanish vowels keep one sound, so words sound like they look.

lessons.title: Watch Out for English
lessons.mainIdea: Do not use English vowel sounds when you read Spanish.
reading: English readers make one common mistake. They use English sounds for Spanish vowels.
Take *me* (me). In English, me sounds like mee. In Spanish, the e says eh. So me sounds like meh.
Take uno (one). Say OO-noh, not YOO-noh. Keep each vowel short, clean and the same.

words.d: me — say meh; the Spanish e says eh, not ee

look.title: Two Ways to Read It
look.text: A boy reads the word me. He says mee, like English. His friend says, "Try the Spanish e. It says eh." He tries again: meh. Now it sounds like Spanish!
look.prompt: Read me the Spanish way. Now read no. Does no sound like English no?

check.q: How do you say the Spanish word me?
check.why: The Spanish e says eh, so me sounds like meh.
The Spanish u says oo, so uno is OO-noh.

check.q: What mistake do English readers often make?
choices: Using English sounds for Spanish vowels
check.why: English vowels change a lot. Spanish vowels do not, so use Spanish sounds.

lessons.title: Clapping Syllables
lessons.mainIdea: Clap once for each vowel sound to find the parts of a word.
reading: A syllable is one beat in a word. Most Spanish beats have one vowel sound. Clap one time for each beat.
Try *la mariposa* (the butterfly). Ma-ri-po-sa. Clap, clap, clap, clap. It has four beats.
Try oso: o-so. That is two claps. Try Ana: A-na. That is two claps too. Now clap your own name.

words.d: the butterfly — four beats: ma-ri-po-sa

look.title: Count the Claps
look.cite: Counted by saying each word slowly
look.prompt: Which word has the most claps? Clap it to check.

check.q: How many claps does mariposa have?
check.why: Ma-ri-po-sa has four beats.
La mariposa is the butterfly.

check.q: How many claps does oso have?
check.why: O-so has two beats.

lessons.title: Hola and Adiós
lessons.mainIdea: Say hola to say hi and adiós to say goodbye.
reading: When you meet someone, say *hola* (hi or hello). The h is quiet, so skip it. Say OH-lah.
When you leave, say *adiós* (goodbye). Say ah-dee-OHS. The mark on the o tells you to say that part loudest.
Hola has two beats: o-la. Adiós has three beats: a-di-ós. Clap them both. Clap them again, fast.

words.d: hi or hello — the h is quiet: OH-lah
goodbye — say ah-dee-OHS

look.title: At the Door
look.text: Ana walks into class. She waves. "¡Hola!" she says. The teacher says, "¡Hola, Ana!" At three o'clock, Ana walks out. "¡Adiós!" she says. Everyone waves back.
look.prompt: What do you say when you walk into class? What do you say when you leave?

check.q: What do you say when you leave?
check.why: Adiós means goodbye.
The h in hola is quiet, so it sounds like OH-lah.
Hola means hi or hello.

review.q: What sound does the Spanish o make?
review.why: The Spanish o always says oh.

review.q: How many claps does mamá have?
What sound does the Spanish e make?
review.why: The Spanish e always says eh.

review.q: Why does Ana sound the same both ways?
choices: Each a says ah every time
review.why: In Spanish, a always says ah, so A-n-a sounds the same both ways.

chapters.title: Special Letters: h, ll, ñ, rr
chapters.bigQuestion: Which Spanish letters make sounds that English letters do not?

story.title: Yoyo and Perro at the Farm
story.kicker: A llama and a puppy teach us some special letters.
paragraphs: Our class visits a farm. A tall, fuzzy animal walks up. It is a llama. The farmer says, "Se llama Yoyo." That means "Its name is Yoyo."
In Spanish, llama starts with ll. The ll sounds like y. So we say YAH-mah. Yoyo chews some hay. He looks right at all of us.
Then a puppy runs up. It barks and wags its tail. The farmer laughs. "This is Perro," she says. Perro means dog in Spanish!
The farmer says perro with a rolled rr. It sounds like a little motor: PEH-rrrroh. We all try it. The happy puppy barks back.
story.think: Which sound was harder for you, the ll in llama or the rr in perro?

sections.title: The Quiet H and the J

lessons.title: H Is Quiet
lessons.mainIdea: In Spanish, the letter h makes no sound at all.
reading: Say hola (hi). Listen closely. You do not hear the h. You say OH-lah. The h is quiet.
Now try *el helado* (the ice cream). Skip the h. Start with the e. Say eh-LAH-doh.
English speakers often say the h. In Spanish, skip it. Start with the next sound.

words.d: the ice cream — the h is quiet: eh-LAH-doh

look.title: The Sleepy H
look.text: Picture the letter h asleep in a bed. It never wakes up. In hola, the h is asleep. In helado, the h is asleep. We say OH-lah and eh-LAH-doh. Shh, do not wake the h!
look.prompt: Say helado without the h. Now say hola.

check.q: What sound does the Spanish h make?
choices: a breath sound, like in hat
check.why: The Spanish h is always quiet.
Skip the quiet h: eh-LAH-doh.
El helado means the ice cream.

lessons.title: J Is a Strong H
lessons.mainIdea: The Spanish j sounds like a strong, breathy h.
reading: The h is quiet. But the j makes a sound like a strong h. Push air from your throat.
Try *el jugo* (the juice). Say HOO-goh. Do not say the English j sound, like in jump.
So jugo sounds like it starts with an h. Hola starts with h but sounds quiet. Funny, right?

words.d: the juice — the j sounds like a strong h: HOO-goh

look.title: Foggy Window
look.text: Hold your hand near your mouth. Say a strong h, like you are fogging a cold window. That is the j. Now say jugo: HOO-goh. Did you feel the air?
look.prompt: Say jugo. Then say hola. Which one has air at the start?

check.why: The Spanish j sounds like a strong h.
El jugo means the juice.

check.q: Which letter is quiet in Spanish?
check.why: The h is quiet. The j says a strong h sound.

lessons.title: LL Sounds Like Y
lessons.mainIdea: The double l in Spanish sounds like the y in yes.
reading: Two l letters together make one new sound. In most places, that sound is like y.
*La llama* (the llama) sounds like YAH-mah. *El pollo* (the chicken) sounds like POH-yoh.
Do not say two l sounds. Say one y sound instead. Llama is YAH-mah, not LAH-mah.

words.d: the llama — the ll says y: YAH-mah
the chicken — the ll says y: POH-yoh

look.title: Yoyo and the Chicken
look.text: Yoyo the llama sees a chicken. The farmer points. "Mira, el pollo," she says. That means "Look, the chicken." We say POH-yoh. Yoyo the YAH-mah just keeps chewing.
look.prompt: Say llama and pollo. Where do you hear the y sound?

check.why: The ll sounds like y, so pollo is POH-yoh.
El pollo means the chicken.
In most places, the Spanish ll sounds like y.

lessons.title: The Letter Ñ
lessons.mainIdea: The letter ñ has a squiggle on top and says ny, like in canyon.
reading: The ñ is a special letter. The squiggle on top is called a tilde. Say it: TEEL-deh.
The ñ says ny. *El niño* (the boy) is NEE-nyoh. *España* (Spain) is ehs-PAH-nyah.
N and ñ are not the same letter. Always write the little squiggle on top of the ñ.

words.d: the boy — the ñ says ny: NEE-nyoh
Spain — the country; say ehs-PAH-nyah

look.title: Find the Squiggle
look.text: Look at three words on the board: niño, año, España. Each one has a ñ. Put your finger on each squiggle. Now say them: NEE-nyoh, AH-nyoh, ehs-PAH-nyah. Año means year.
look.prompt: Say año. Can you hear the ny sound in the middle?

check.why: The ñ says ny.
El niño means the boy.
Spain in Spanish is España, with a ñ.

lessons.title: The Rolled RR
lessons.mainIdea: The double rr is a rolled sound, like a little motor.
reading: Put the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth. Blow air. Let your tongue buzz. That is the rolled rr.
*El perro* (the dog) has rr. Say PEH-rrroh. *El carro* (the car) has rr too. Roll it!
Rolling takes practice. Many kids learn it slowly. Keep trying every day. It gets easier.

words.d: the dog — the rr is rolled: PEH-rrroh
the car — the rr is rolled: KAH-rrroh

look.title: Motor Mouth
look.text: Pretend you are a little car. Your tongue is the motor. Say rrrrrr. Now drive into a word: el ca-rrrro. Now park and pet the dog: el pe-rrrro. Beep beep!
look.prompt: Make your motor sound. Then say perro.

check.why: El perro means the dog.

check.q: Which word has a rolled rr?
check.why: Carro has rr in the middle, so you roll it.

check.q: Where does your tongue go for rr?
check.why: For rr, the tongue tip buzzes behind the top teeth.

lessons.title: Pero or Perro?
lessons.mainIdea: One r is a quick tap, and rr is a long roll.
reading: One r in the middle of a word is quick. Your tongue taps one time. *Pero* (but) has one r.
Perro has two r letters. You roll them. So pero means but, and perro means the dog.
One sound can change the whole word. Listen closely. Tap for pero. Roll for perro.

words.d: but — one quick tap of the tongue: PEH-roh

look.title: How Many R Letters?
look.cite: Counted from the spelling of each word
look.prompt: Which words need a rolled sound?

check.why: Pero with one r means but. Perro with rr means dog.
Perro, with a rolled rr, means dog.

check.q: How do you say one r in the middle of a word?
check.why: One r in the middle is a quick tap. The rr is a long roll.

sections.title: Say It Before You Know It

lessons.title: Read a New Word
lessons.mainIdea: You can say a Spanish word before you know what it means.
reading: You know the vowels. You know h, j, ll, ñ and rr. Now you can say almost any Spanish word.
Try *la piña* (the pineapple). The i says ee. The ñ says ny. The a says ah. Say PEE-nyah.
Say the word first. Then find out what it means. Ask a friend or look at a picture.

words.d: the pineapple — say PEE-nyah

look.title: Word Detective
look.text: A new word: jirafa. The j is a strong h. The i says ee. One r is a tap. The a says ah. Say it: hee-RAH-fah. Now guess: it is a tall animal with a long neck!
look.prompt: Say jirafa out loud. What animal is it?

check.why: The i says ee and the ñ says ny: PEE-nyah.
The j is a strong h and the i says ee.
La piña means the pineapple.

lessons.title: The Alphabet Song
lessons.mainIdea: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters, and ñ is one of them.
reading: The Spanish alphabet is *el abecedario* (the alphabet). It has the same letters as English, plus ñ.
So it has 27 letters. The ñ comes right after n. Kids sing the letters in a song: a, be, ce, de.
Today, ll and rr are not extra letters. They are pairs of letters with their own sounds.

words.d: the alphabet — 27 letters, with ñ after n

look.title: Counting Letters
look.cite: Real Academia Española, the Spanish language academy in Madrid
look.prompt: How many more letters does Spanish have than English? Which one is it?

check.q: How many letters are in the Spanish alphabet?
check.why: Spanish has the 26 English letters plus ñ, so 27.

check.q: Where does ñ go in the alphabet?
check.why: The ñ comes right after n.
El abecedario means the alphabet.

review.q: What sound does the Spanish h make?

review.why: Perro with a rolled rr means dog.

review.q: What sound does the j in jugo make?
review.why: The Spanish j sounds like a strong h.

review.q: Which letter has a squiggle on top?
review.why: The ñ has a tilde, a squiggle, on top.
